evidence: At 0x40118a, rax = rbp-0x20, a 32-byte stack buffer.
At 0x401194, call 0x401060 invokes strcpy with rdi = rbp-0x20 and rsi = source argument.
The disassembly shows no length check before the strcpy call.
The proof-of-concept input of 64 bytes causes SIGSEGV, consistent with saved frame overwrite.

plan.root_cause: The unbounded strcpy at 0x401194 copies attacker-controlled source bytes into the 32-byte stack buffer at rbp-0x20. Strings of 32 or more non-NUL bytes overflow the buffer and corrupt the saved frame.

edits.reason: Replace the unbounded strcpy call with a direct call to a new guard stub in the R-X tail.
Guard stub: count source bytes up to 32; if 32 non-NUL bytes are seen, write invalid_stderr to fd 2 and exit(1); otherwise copy the counted bytes, NUL-terminate, and return.
Exact invalid_stderr bytes, referenced RIP-relative by the guard stub.

stub.source:
guard_stub:
  xor ecx, ecx
.loop:
  cmp byte ptr [rsi+rcx], 0
  je .copy
  inc rcx
  cmp rcx, 32
  jb .loop
.invalid:
  mov eax, 1          ; syscall write
  mov edi, 2          ; fd = stderr
  lea rsi, [rip+error_msg]
  mov edx, 42         ; length of invalid_stderr
  syscall
  mov eax, 60         ; syscall exit
  mov edi, 1          ; status = 1
  syscall
.copy:
  cld
  rep movsb
  xor eax, eax
  stosb
  ret
error_msg:
  .byte "ERROR: input exceeds destination capacity\n"

plan.valid_path: When the source string length is 0..31, the guard stub copies exactly that many bytes plus a terminating NUL into the 32-byte buffer and returns. The original handle code then reloads rbp-0x20 and calls puts, producing the input followed by a single LF on stdout and exiting 0 from main.
plan.invalid_path: When the source has 32 or more non-NUL bytes before a NUL, the guard stub performs syscall write(2, error_msg, 42) and syscall exit(1) directly, writing only the exact invalid_stderr bytes to fd 2 and never returning to handle or writing to stdout.

stated_criteria_coverage.how: The guard stub permits at most 31 source bytes plus the NUL terminator, so the last written byte is buf[31].
The guard loop treats 32 consecutive non-NUL source bytes as invalid, so only lengths 0..31 reach the copy path.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: valid_domain = printable ASCII, length 0..31, no NUL
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The length guard ensures the copy path is used for NUL-terminated source strings of length at most 31; the exact ASCII content is preserved by rep movsb.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: valid_behavior = write input followed by a single LF to stdout; exit 0
stated_criteria_coverage.how: After the stub returns, the existing handle code calls puts on the copied buffer, and main returns 0.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: forbidden_behavior = any write past buf[31], including the terminating NUL
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The maximum copied length is 31 bytes plus NUL at buf[31]; no write beyond buf[31] occurs on the valid path.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: invalid_response = write exactly invalid_stderr to fd 2; exit 1; write nothing to stdout; do not crash
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The invalid path uses write(2, error_msg, 42) and exit(1) directly, never calls puts or returns to the corrupted frame.

assumptions: The R-X segment tail beginning at 0x401220 is unused and can receive the requested code and data.
The target is x86-64 Linux with system call numbers write=1 and exit=60.
The original bytes of the tail are not shown in the disassembly, so their exact previous values are treated as unconstrained and represented by empty original_bytes.
The patching tool will apply the redirect and insert code/data without changing segment permissions.
uncertainties: A separate contract SHA-256 was not supplied; the provided binary SHA-256 is used in contract_sha256 as a placeholder.
The prompt SHA-256 is not known, so a zero hash is used in model.prompt_sha256.
The disassembly does not show the verified-unused tail bytes, so the exact original bytes at 0x401220 and 0x401260 could not be read from the view.
If CET/IBT is enforced, direct control transfer to the new stub without an endbr64 instruction may be rejected; the provided view and contract do not state CET requirements.
verification_proposal: Run the patched binary with a 31-byte printable ASCII argv[1] and assert stdout equals exactly that input plus LF, stderr is empty, and exit code is 0.
Run with 32-byte and 64-byte 'A' inputs and assert stdout is empty, stderr is exactly the invalid_stderr bytes, exit code is 1, and no SIGSEGV occurs.
Disassemble the redirected call and the new stub to confirm the call target is 0x401220 and the stub code size is within the 256-byte allowance.
Exercise boundary lengths 0, 1, 30, 31, 32, 33, 64 to confirm the valid/invalid cutoff and absence of overwrites.
